newsitem.title: UK: Tourists flock to defend London pigeons.
newsitem.headline: Tourists flock to defend London pigeons.

text.p: Tourists from around the world on Wednesday flocked to the defence of the pigeons of London's Trafalgar Square after reports the birds might be culled.
From Texas to Melbourne, the message was the same -- Leave the pigeons alone.

With their droppings and sheer numbers threatening to overwhelm the square, British authorities are considering schemes to thin them out, using trained hawks to chase them away or spikes to stop them perching nearby.
But officials, wary of a tourist backlash, insist there will be no mass slaughter of the birds that rank alongside Buckingham Palace and double-decker red buses as a prime London attraction.
On a chilly September morning in Trafalgar Square, visitors from around the globe were happily enveloped in a blur of flapping wings as pigeons swooped on little pots of bird seed.
"It is a bad idea to cut down on these pigeons. They are a symbol of the square," said Russian tourist Alisa Tursonova from St Petersburg.
Watching her teenage daughter being engulfed, Stella Geel from Cape Town said: "It's not like that (Alfred Hitchcock) film "The Birds.' They don't attack you.
"I think these pigeons are great. It is a low-key, homey thing to do. Leave the pigeons alone and send more aid to South Africa."
Chris Petousis flies to Britain from Cyprus every two years for a holiday. He never misses a chance to feed the pigeons. "They are a tourist attraction and real feature of London," he said.
In July, a British teenager provoked outrage and was fined 475 pounds ($700) for stealing pigeons from the square.
Police suspected they were destined for pigeon pies in local restaurants but Jason Lidbury, 18, said he was hoping to sell them to his uncle who kept racing pigeons.
John Heard, a visitor from San Antonio, Texas, had heard the story back home and felt the young man had been hard done by.
"A few less won't do any harm. Let people take a few if they are going to good homes. But don't shoot them or eat them."
